conventions: * Muhurta Chintamani (Vivaha and Griha prakaranas) as summarised by B.V. Raman, *Muhurtha*: the lagna is the most powerful corrective; combust Venus or Jupiter forbids a marriage outright. * Common almanac lists are used for each event's nakshatras, tithis and weekdays. Almanacs differ in a few entries; the lists used are returned with the result so the reader can name them. * Lahiri ayanamsa; the Vedic weekday runs sunrise to sunrise (centre of the disc, standard refraction). * Rahu Kalam, Yamaganda and Gulika Kalam are the customary eighth-parts of daylight by weekday. * Tarabala: count from the person's birth nakshatra to the day's; remainders 3, 5 and 7 (Vipat, Pratyari, Vadha) fail. Chandrabala: the transiting Moon in the 1st, 3rd, 6th, 7th, 10th or 11th from the birth Moon sign passes; in Shukla paksha the 2nd, 5th and 9th also pass (the waxing Moon's relaxation in the muhurta texts). * Avoided weekdays (Tuesday and Saturday for marriage) are a penalty by default, because North Indian almanac lists use them freely; --weekday-rule hard rejects them outright for families who follow the stricter rule. * Kharmas (Sun in sidereal Sagittarius or Pisces) is avoided for marriage and griha pravesh, as in North Indian practice. Chaturmas (lunar, Devshayani to Prabodhini Ekadashi) is NOT applied; mention it if the family follows it. * Tithis in the event lists are counted within each paksha (1 to 15; 15 = Purnima). Rikta (4, 9, 14) and Amavasya are always rejected; the 8th and Purnima are rejected where the event list says so (B.V. Raman for marriage). * Never promise an outcome. A good muhurta supports a beginning; it does not guarantee results.
